assessment.nobel_worthiness: Halide perovskites turned a soft, solution-processable ionic crystal into a photovoltaic absorber with efficiencies that rose from a few percent to above 25 percent in a decade. It is a materials discovery in which composition, crystal structure and defect tolerance explain function, and it has reshaped solar, LED and detector research worldwide.
assessment.attribution: Miyasaka reported the first perovskite-sensitized cell (2009); Park's solid-state cell (2012) and Snaith's meso-superstructured cell (2012) established the high-efficiency architecture. Grätzel, Seok, and Kanatzidis made major contributions too, so any three-person choice excludes strong contributors.
assessment.maturity: Reproduced in thousands of laboratories with independent certified efficiencies, but stability, lead toxicity and commercialization are unresolved. Recognition is timely on impact, arguably early on technological maturity.
uncertainties: Which three of six strong contributors is fair; the field's precedence history is contested.
Long-term operational stability is not yet demonstrated at scale.
Possible overlap with a physics or energy-oriented framing; my knowledge of the credit details is not independently verified.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Surfactant-templated ordered mesoporous silicas (MCM-41, FSM-16, SBA-15) opened pore sizes of 2-50 nm with long-range order, beyond zeolites. This is a clear, original synthetic concept based on cooperative self-assembly, and it has spawned ordered mesoporous carbons, metal oxides and catalytic supports. The structure was proven by diffraction and electron microscopy.
assessment.attribution: The Mobil group (Kresge, Beck and colleagues) reported MCM-41 in 1992; Inagaki and Kuroda independently made FSM-16 earlier or in parallel. Ryoo, Zhao and Stucky extended the field with new structures (MCM-48, SBA-15, ordered carbons). Credit is spread and priority between the Japanese and Mobil work is delicate.
assessment.maturity: More than thirty years of confirmation and broad use in catalysis, adsorption and drug delivery. Recognition is mature, though the largest commercial impact has been modest compared with zeolites.
uncertainties: Priority and fair weighting between Mobil and Waseda/Toyota work.
Whether Ryoo, Zhao or Stucky should be included over Beck.
Industrial impact is less decisive than for other candidates.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Nitrogenase is the enzyme that makes biological nitrogen fixation possible. Crystal structures of the MoFe protein with its FeMo-cofactor, then the interstitial carbide and mechanistic trapping of intermediates, give atomic-level answers to a fundamental chemical question. The work is structurally rigorous and links inorganic cluster chemistry to biology.
assessment.attribution: Rees solved the first MoFe protein structure and later resolved the central carbide; Einsle's high-resolution structure and the follow-up structural work on turnover states were decisive; Dean and Seefeldt contributed genetics and biochemistry, and Ribbe the cofactor biosynthesis. Choosing three is difficult.
assessment.maturity: The structural picture is well confirmed, but the full catalytic mechanism (which atoms bind N2, the role of the belt sulfur displacement) is still debated, so recognition may be somewhat early for mechanism, though ripe for structure.
uncertainties: Mechanism of N2 reduction is not settled.
Allocation among Rees, Einsle, Dean, Seefeldt and Ribbe is unresolved.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Serial femtosecond crystallography at X-ray free-electron lasers allows structures of nano- and microcrystals at room temperature and time-resolved structural movies of reactions, a clear enabling method that solves the radiation-damage limit. It resonates strongly with my own interest in structure from tiny crystals.
assessment.attribution: Chapman led the 2011 proof-of-principle with Fromme, Schlichting and colleagues; Hajdu was the conceptual originator of diffraction-before-destruction. Other pioneers outside the list (for example Neutze) are not available in credited names, which complicates fair attribution.
assessment.maturity: Methods are validated and widely adopted, with several independent facilities, though access is limited and large-scale routine impact on chemistry is still developing. Timing is reasonable.
uncertainties: Concept versus experimental realization credit is contested and some key people are not in the credited list.
Overlap with physics or biology framing.
Facility-limited availability narrows impact.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Base editing converts one DNA base to another without double-strand breaks, using engineered deaminases fused to Cas proteins. It is a creative chemical-biology design with demonstrated therapeutic relevance and has already entered clinical use, with very strong lasting impact on genome engineering.
assessment.attribution: Liu conceived and led the work, with Komor and Gaudelli as the principal first authors; a single-laureate award to Liu is the cleanest configuration. Kondo and Nishida's independent cytidine deaminase work is a real parallel contribution.
assessment.maturity: Clinical evidence is arriving, and independent confirmation is extensive, though the Chemistry prize for CRISPR (2020) already covered genome editing, which lowers the novelty margin.
uncertainties: Committee may regard it as downstream of the 2020 CRISPR prize.
Independent contribution of Kondo and Nishida complicates a single-name award.
Long-term clinical safety data are still limited.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: MXenes are a large family of two-dimensional transition-metal carbides and nitrides made by selective etching of MAX phases, with tunable composition, surface terminations and conductivity. They give a new materials class with applications in energy storage, shielding and catalysis, and the structure has been confirmed by diffraction and electron microscopy.
assessment.attribution: Naguib, Gogotsi and Barsoum with colleagues reported Ti3C2 in 2011 and the family followed. The three credited names map naturally to a fair prize, though the Drexel group extension and other contributors are not separately captured.
assessment.maturity: More than a decade of reproduction worldwide with thousands of compositions, but practical applications are still emerging, so the recognition would be somewhat early.
uncertainties: Applications and commercial outcomes are not yet proven.
Surface termination structure remains heterogeneous and incompletely controlled.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Atomic layer deposition gives self-limiting, conformal thin films with atomic control and is essential in microelectronics manufacturing, batteries and catalysts. The industrial and scientific impact is large and lasting, and the chemistry of surface-limited reactions is clear.
assessment.attribution: Suntola invented the process (as atomic layer epitaxy) in the 1970s; George and Leskelä built the general chemistry and materials breadth. Puurunen's historical work on the earlier Soviet molecular layering is a notable attribution complication.
assessment.maturity: Very mature and widely confirmed, with decades of industrial use. Timing is more than ripe, though the discovery is more a process than a single conceptual advance.
uncertainties: Earlier molecular layering work in the Soviet Union complicates priority.
Whether it is seen as chemistry or engineering.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Supported single-atom catalysts maximize atom efficiency and make active sites structurally defined, with direct evidence from aberration-corrected HAADF-STEM and X-ray absorption. The concept links heterogeneous catalysis to molecular-level structure, which I value, and it has spread across catalysis and electrocatalysis.
assessment.attribution: The 2011 Nature Chemistry paper from Zhang, Qiao, Wang and colleagues coined the concept and framed the field, and the credited names reflect that group. Earlier work on isolated sites by others complicates novelty and the first demonstration.
assessment.maturity: The field is young and some claims of true single-atom sites and stability are disputed, with a risk of overinterpretation; independent confirmation is substantial but the practical industrial impact is still limited, so it is likely premature.
uncertainties: Characterization sometimes cannot distinguish single atoms from clusters or ensembles.
Industrial relevance and durability are not yet established.
Prior isolated-site work may reduce originality.
